title: The Harmonic Color-Rising

features.name: the rising chorus
features.desc-on-touch: You hear children's voices made visible—each note a strand of light, rising in harmony. The colors are their names written in sound that climbed too far to stay sound.

features.name: waves of old singing
features.desc-on-touch: The archive remembers every chorus that ever sang back to it. This wave holds three hundred voices from a hundred springs—a mountain of sound made visible at last.

features.name: the school-hall glyph
features.desc-on-touch: A plaque marks where the town's children stood in rows to sing on spring evenings. Their voices learned to climb. The archive heard them and learned to answer.

features.name: the first light-note
features.desc-on-touch: This is the moment the singing reached so high that the archive stopped hearing it as sound. It became something the archive could only see—a threshold where meaning learned a new frequency.

features.name: the recording that answered back
features.desc-on-touch: A file that sang to the archive and received singing in return. Now it holds both conversations layered as light, the voices calling and being called to across years.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the school hall at singing hour
narr: You stood at the back of the hall with her,
watching the children sing something old and local.
Her hand found yours. The song rose higher
than should fit in that small space. She said:
"The archive is singing back." You felt it then—
the air itself learning a name for what was rising.

inscription: the voices of every chorus ever sung, learning together that sound can become light when it rises high enough to remember the sky
